title: IS12:: goodswap.c (14.1)

lines.code: Objective: use of addresses in function arguments

lines.explanation: Function prototype for a bad swap example.
Function prototype for a good swap example, with pointers.
This printf statements outputs the original values.
The results of the bad swap are printed out.  Nothing is switched.  That's because they were only switched locally, and the original values for the parameters are returned.
The results of the good swap are printed out.  It is successful because it uses pointers.  The value of the parameter is left the same, but the value it CONTAINS is switched successfully.

lines.code: /* bad example of swapping - a function can't change parameters */

lines.explanation: This function looks like it is swapping values, in the same manner used for sorts.  However, it is only within the function.  When a value is returned, the parameters retain the same values.

lines.code: /*    good example of swapping - a function can't change prameters
but if a parameter is a pointer it can change the value it points to */

lines.explanation: This function also swaps values using apparently the same method as in the bad swap.  However, it doesn't swap the parameters, it swaps the contents that are stored at the addresses they are pointing to.  This is successful (see output).
